scope: General noncommercial Class C licensing guidance; not an individualized eligibility determination.

rules.title: Adult education ages 18–24
requirements: Complete six-hour adult driver education; full teen-course alternatives are described by TDLR.
required_certificates: Adult education completion evidence (ADE-1317 for adult six-hour course)

rules.title: No mandatory education at 25+
requirements: DPS states no driver education requirement at ages 25 and older. Driving lessons remain optional preparation.

rules.title: Usual first-time tests and application
requirements: Apply at DPS, provide required documents and biometrics, pay the application fee, and pass vision, knowledge and driving skills requirements unless an applicable waiver is established.

rules.title: Testing versus issuance
requirements: Testing may be completed through an eligible third-party provider. DPS completes license issuance; a test pass alone is not a license.

evidence.section_locator: Once your driver license has been issued

rules.title: Start education at 14, learner at 15
requirements: Classroom education may begin at 14; a learner license requires age 15 or older.

rules.title: Teen classroom total has conflicting official wording
requirements: Current overview pages and ITTD FAQ describe 24 classroom hours; TDLR learner/block and hybrid pages still say 32. Do not quote one universal total or completion schedule until TDLR/provider review.

rules.title: Concurrent learner classroom milestone
requirements: Complete the first six classroom hours and obtain the learner-stage education certificate before applying to DPS.

rules.title: Block learner milestone needs review
requirements: Block method completes all classroom instruction before the learner application; the official 24/32-hour discrepancy must be resolved for the selected course.

rules.title: Supervising adult
requirements: Drive only with a licensed adult aged at least 21 in the front passenger seat.

rules.title: Holding period
requirements: Hold the learner license at least six months unless turning 18 first. Suspension extends the holding period by the suspension duration.

rules.title: Learner validity
requirements: The teen learner license expires on the 18th birthday; confirm the next DPS application rather than assuming automatic conversion.

rules.title: Teen school attendance evidence
requirements: Bring diploma/GED or Verification of Enrollment and Attendance. VOE is valid for 30 days, or 90 days when issued June through August.

rules.title: Teen guardian and education evidence
requirements: Bring the applicable DE-964/DEE-964/DE-964E education evidence and required identity, residency, lawful-status and SSN documentation. Parent/guardian presence or an accepted waiver/notarized application is required as specified by DPS.

rules.title: In-car instruction and practice are separate
requirements: Complete seven hours driving instruction, seven observation hours, and 30 additional supervised practice hours including ten at night. A school package is not automatically all 44 hours.

rules.title: Practice supervision and log
requirements: The practice supervisor must be 21+, licensed for at least a year; the parent/guardian certifies the 30-hour practice log. Follow the approved course instructions for other logs.

rules.title: Usual teen road-test prerequisites
requirements: Complete classroom and in-car education, the applicable learner holding period and ITTD within 90 days, then pass the skills test; DPS decides provisional issuance.

rules.title: Provisional passenger and nighttime restrictions
requirements: No more than one non-family passenger under 21. No driving midnight–5 a.m. except work, school activities or emergencies.

rules.title: Device restriction
requirements: Cellphone use, including hands-free, is prohibited while driving except an emergency under the cited teen guidance.

rules.title: PTDE authorization and guide
requirements: Obtain TDLR instructor designation for the particular student before teaching; read the supplied program guide and select an approved parent-taught course.

rules.title: TDLR designation fee
requirements: Current public guidance states $20 nonrefundable per instructor/student designation application, online only. This is separate from course costs.

rules.title: Instructor relationships
requirements: Eligible relationships include parent, stepparent, grandparent, step-grandparent, foster parent and legal guardian. An authorized alternate must meet the same qualifications and may not charge a fee.

rules.title: Instructor screening is not approval
requirements: The official eligibility questionnaire asks age 25+, seven years holding a license, three continuous valid-license years, homicide/DWI history, suspensions, accidents and moving violations. These are screening questions; obtain TDLR/DPS confirmation of the actual instructor's eligibility.

rules.title: DPS record checks and B restriction
requirements: B-restricted license holders cannot instruct. DPS checks the instructor's record at learner and provisional stages; disqualification may invalidate subsequent instruction hours.

rules.title: No driving instruction before learner issuance
requirements: Obtain the learner license before starting behind-the-wheel training; finish remaining classroom and in-car requirements afterward.

rules.title: PTDE daily instruction limits conflict
requirements: TDLR classroom guidance permits six daily instruction hours, while the in-car page caps combined classroom/in-car credit at two. Do not calculate completion dates until TDLR resolves the discrepancy.

evidence.section_locator: two hours per day of instruction

rules.title: Hybrid transfer needs course review
requirements: TDLR describes transfer of licensed-school classroom education into parent-taught in-car instruction after designation. The page's 32-hour classroom wording conflicts with 24-hour overviews; confirm course acceptance and transfer certificate.

rules.title: Approved education options
requirements: Use an approved driver education provider, an eligible public-school course or authorized PTDE pathway. Confirm the provider's relevant approval/endorsement before choosing an online or parent-taught course.

rules.title: Turning 18 during teen education
requirements: Partial teen classroom hours cannot be credited toward the six-hour adult course. Complete the full teen program or full adult course.

rules.title: Education transfers and duplicate certificates
requirements: Contact the original approved provider for duplicate certificates. Texas-licensed school transfers are possible; out-of-state education hours do not transfer under TDLR guidance—confirm the licensing scenario with DPS.

rules.title: ITD is separate from education
requirements: Complete the appropriate ITD program after required education/in-car instruction and before skills testing. It does not replace driver education.

evidence.section_locator: prior to taking the driving skills test

rules.title: Usual minor ITTD and adult ITAD
requirements: Minor teen/PTDE applicants use ITTD (two hours). Adult six-hour-course/ADE-1317 applicants use ITAD (one hour); DPS overview also identifies ITAD for ages 25+.

rules.title: ITD validity and paper copy
requirements: Present a printed ITD certificate dated within 90 days of the skills test. If the test is not passed within that window, restart the program. ITAD and ITTD are free.
required_documents: Printed ITD completion certificate within 90 days

rules.title: Adult ITD selection ambiguity
requirements: Adult FAQ permits either ITAD or ITTD at 18+, while the overview and certificate-based FAQs specify programs differently. Confirm the acceptable program with DPS/testing provider for adults holding teen certificates; do not invent a universal choice.

rules.title: Core application document categories
requirements: Provide identity, Texas residency, citizenship/lawful-presence evidence and SSN as applicable, plus the application. Owned-vehicle insurance or a no-vehicle statement is specified; vehicle registration evidence at application is limited to new residents exchanging out-of-state licenses on the general DPS page.
required_documents: Owned-vehicle registration for new-resident out-of-state exchange

rules.title: Identity combinations
requirements: Use one primary identity document, two secondary, or one secondary plus two supporting. Present originals/certified copies and legal name-change evidence when needed; photocopies are not accepted.
required_documents: One primary OR two secondary OR one secondary plus two supporting identity documents

rules.title: Texas residency documents
requirements: Normally present two printed documents with the applicant's name and Texas residential address; one must show at least 30 days' residency. Exchange of a valid unexpired out-of-state license/ID waives the 30-day duration, not the two-document requirement.
required_documents: Two printed named Texas-address residency documents, subject to DPS exceptions

rules.title: Residency affidavit option
requirements: DPS provides a conditional residency-affidavit option and special cases. Confirm the appropriate affidavit and supporting documentation with DPS; it is not a blanket exemption.

rules.title: SSN verification
requirements: DPS electronically verifies SSN information; resolve mismatches with SSA before issuance.

rules.title: SSN ineligibility affidavit
requirements: DPS describes an office SSN affidavit for ineligible applicants. The page's never-applied/applied-and-denied wording is ambiguous; have DPS confirm eligibility and required evidence.

rules.title: Lawful presence verification
requirements: Present appropriate lawful-status evidence for the applicant category. DHS verification must complete before DPS issues the license; no approval or immigration outcome is guaranteed.

rules.title: DPS test vehicle safety
requirements: Bring a legally operable vehicle that passes the examiner's safety check: working signals, horn, speedometer, mirrors, doors, seatbelts and brake lights, plus weather-appropriate lights/wipers. Bring current registration and insurance; the applicant must not be an excluded driver.

rules.title: Test-day identification and failure triggers
requirements: Present valid identification. Unsafe vehicles may prevent testing; pets/unauthorized passengers are excluded, and dangerous or illegal maneuvers cause an automatic failure.

rules.title: Annual inspection versus examiner safety check
requirements: DPS says annual noncommercial safety inspection ended January 1, 2025, while March 2026 DL-60 still lists unexpired inspection for testing. The examiner safety check remains separate; confirm exact test-vehicle paperwork with DPS/provider and do not promise a universal annual-inspection requirement.

rules.title: Teen post-test submission
requirements: DL-68 describes submitting third-party results in a sealed unaltered envelope with applicable provisional documents and completed classroom/in-car certificates. Confirm whether the specific approved provider uses an authorized digital process instead.
required_documents: Third-party test results via confirmed accepted handoff

rules.title: Provider-specific testing gate remains unverified
requirements: DPS and TDLR support third-party skills testing generally, but the TPST program page and DL-65 could not be reviewed. Confirm current adult restricted-license prerequisites and the school's active testing authorization before booking.

rules.title: Resident driving deadline
requirements: DPS permits driving with a valid unexpired US-state/territory, Canadian or qualifying-country license for up to 90 days after moving to Texas.

rules.title: Usual adult valid US transfer
requirements: Surrender the recognized license and apply with Texas documents. DPS describes knowledge/skills and adult education/ITD waivers; do not sell a first-time education or test package as mandatory.

rules.title: Expired out-of-state adult license
requirements: DPS moving guidance describes waivers for licenses expired not over two years, and DL-60 reserves DPS discretion to require a test. Confirm expiry dates and the actual application before recommending a waiver.

rules.title: Minor transfer conflict
requirements: Moving guidance says valid surrendered licenses/permits receive the equivalent Texas version; GDL guidance says all transfers obtain a Texas learner and hold six months. All minors need skills testing, but the exact transfer stage/holding requirement requires DPS confirmation.

rules.title: Foreign reciprocal license categories
requirements: DPS lists France, Germany, South Korea, UAE and Taiwan for valid-license testing reciprocity; retaining the foreign license affects waivers. Confirm the applicant's age, country, license validity and surrender choice with DPS.

rules.title: Foreign document translations
requirements: DPS requires foreign licenses not in English or Spanish to be translated by a translation service or consulate; foreign marriage documents not in English need certified English translation.

rules.title: Visitors versus residents
requirements: Recognition of a foreign license depends on agreements and nonresident conditions; DPS describes a limited visitor period and a different 90-day resident rule. Ask residency and country; confirm individual recognition and IDP questions with DPS.

rules.title: Hardship license exception
requirements: DPS describes a necessity-based minor restricted/hardship license with an exception to the six-month learner hold and expiry at the next birthday. DPS must establish the qualifying hardship; do not infer approval.

rules.title: Military/NATO exceptions
requirements: DPS describes conditional military-extension and NATO-order testing exemptions. Route documentation and applicability to DPS rather than promising a waiver.

rules.title: Adult permit and waiting-period gap
requirements: The six-month holding rule is verified for minors, not automatically adults. Exact adult restricted-license acquisition and third-party test prerequisites remain unverified in this snapshot; confirm with DPS/provider.

rules.title: Provisional expiry versus restrictions
requirements: TDLR's step guide says the provisional license expires at 18 and must be renewed. Confirm the exact expiry of each restriction with DPS; turning 18 does not itself renew an expired document.

distinctions.license: DPS-issued driving credential subject to its restrictions
